sections.title: Israel's Journey Through Edom
observations: In this section, we see the Israelites being instructed to avoid conflict with the Edomites, descendants of Esau. God reminds them that He has given Edom their land, and they are to respect that boundary. This teaches us about the importance of respecting the sovereignty of others and the boundaries God has set.
The Israelites are reminded of their own journey and hardships, which serves as a lesson in humility and dependence on God. They are to remember that their journey is guided by God's providence.

sections.title: The Wilderness Experience
observations: As the Israelites continue their journey, they are reminded of the long period spent in the wilderness. This serves as a reminder of God's discipline and the necessity of patience in the face of trials.
The mention of the 'forty years' emphasizes the significance of this period in shaping the character of the Israelites. It was a time of testing and preparation for entering the Promised Land.

sections.title: Conquest of the Amorites
observations: God commands the Israelites to engage the Amorites, indicating a shift from avoidance to action. This reflects God's sovereignty in directing the course of history and His plans for Israel.
The defeat of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, is a demonstration of God's power and faithfulness to His promises. It reassures the Israelites of God's presence as they face their enemies.

sections.title: The Land of the Giants
observations: The mention of the giants, the Anakim, serves to highlight the challenges that lie ahead for the Israelites. It reminds them that while the obstacles may seem insurmountable, God is greater than any foe they may encounter.
This section encourages believers to trust in God's strength and not to be intimidated by the size of their challenges.

importantVerses.commentary: For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He knows your going through this great wilderness. These forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.
This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the nations under the whole heaven, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you.

questions: What does this chapter teach us about God's guidance in our lives during difficult times?
How can we apply the lessons of humility and respect for others' boundaries in our own lives?
What does the mention of giants and formidable foes teach us about facing our own challenges?
In what ways can we see God's providence in our own journeys, similar to the Israelites' experience?
